Order 
Heard on I.A.No.8630/2024, an application for dispensing with service on respondents No.1 and 2.
Counsel for the appellant submits that the respondents No.1 and 2 were exparte before the claims Tribunal.
Considering the above the application is allowed.
The service of notice on respondents No.1 and 2 is dispensed with.
Heard finally with the consent of parties.

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 01.12.2022 passed in Claim Case No.3315/2021, whereby challenging quantum of compensation.
The liability of the Insurance Company due to accident by the insured vehicle is not under dispute.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25032 2 MA-65-2023 2.
Short facts of the case are that on 21.10.2021 at around 4.45 in the afternoon appellant Anil was going by his motorcycle.

When he reached near Sonkatch Square on Narsinghgarh Highway, truck container No.RJ-19-GD- 0519 came, which was being driven by its Driver in rash and negligent manner and rammed into the motorcycle of appellant, because of which he sustained grievous injuries on various parts of his body, his left was amputed from above the knee.
He remained hospitalized in Hamidia Hospital, Bhopal and then Medi Plus Hospital, Indore.

sentences.text: The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

The claims Tribunal after considering evidence available on record awarded compensation of Rs.9,67,680/- for loss of earning capacity and after awarding amount in other heads total compensation of Rs.13,58,249/- was awarded.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claims Tribunal has taken the permanent disability with respect to loss of earning capacity at 60% in terms of findings recorded in para 21 of the impugned award.

He submits that Dr. Ashish Mehrotra (AW-2) stated in his statement before the Tribuanl that appellant sustained permanent disability to the extent of 80% due to amputation of his left leg from above knee.
He also refers to Ex.P/74, which is permanent disability certificate issued by the District Medical Board, Indore.

Learned counsel further points out that the claims Tribunal has discarded the claim of income of the appellant, which he stated at Rs.10,000/- per month by doing work of Cooker and Gas repairing and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25032 3 MA-65-2023 Mason.
The claims Tribunal has notionally taken his income at Rs.6,000/- per month treating him as unskilled labour.

Learned counsel, however, points out that even if the income is to be taken on notional basis it should have been Rs.8,800/- per month in view the prescribed minimum wages at the relevant time by the State Legal State Authority.
Thus, he prays for enhancement of compensation.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the claims Tribunal has correctly assessed income of the appellant on notional basis at Rs.6,000/- per month because there was no material at all for proving his income at Rs.10,000/- per month.
As regards permanent disability he points out that the claims Tribunal in para 23 of the award has considered statement of Dr. Ashish Mehrotra (AW-2) in which he himself has opined it to be 60%.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

6. From perusal of Ex.P/74 issued by the District Medical Board, Indore it is clear that appellant has been certified to suffer 80% permanent disability in his left lower limb due to amputation above knee.

Now the question, which has to be considered by the Court is that to what extent this would affect the earning capacity of the appellant keeping in mind he has been treated as unskilled labour in terms of para 27 of the award.

It is also significant to note here that even the Doctor AW-2,
whome the appellat brought before the Tribuanl opined that this 80% permanent disability of left lower limb can be taken as 60% for overall body.

However, looking to the nature of work the appellant used do before the accident, i.e. of Gas and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25032 4 MA-65-2023 Cooker repair and labourer, the permanent disability with respect to loss of earning capacity is taken at 65%.

As regards income of the appellant in terms of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority minimum wages for unskilled Labour were Rs.8,800/- per month, which is taken as income of the appellant.

As such, the compensation for loss of earning capacity in view of the above submissions would change to Rs. 15,37,536/- and after deducting already awarded amount of Rs.9,67,680/- the appellant is now entitled for payment of Rs.5,69,856/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.

2 amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing claim application till its payment.

7. It is seen from the record that the appellant has valued this appeal at Rs.5,00,000/-, thus he is required to pay the deficit Court fees within a period of four weeks.
8.
In view of the above, the present Misc.Appeal stands disposed off.
